q.q: Which of these is software?
q.why: Chrome is a program, so it is software; the others are physical hardware.

q.q: What is hardware?
o: The websites a computer can connect to
The programs and instructions a computer runs
The data a computer stores in its memory
The physical parts of a computer you can touch
q.why: Hardware is the physical parts you can touch; software is the programs.

q.q: In the body analogy, what is software compared to?
q.why: Hardware is like your body; software is like your thoughts and knowledge.

q.q: What happens to the data in memory when the computer is turned off?
o: It moves to the storage device
It is sent to the printer
q.why: Memory is short term and is lost when the computer is turned off.

q.q: Which is an output device?
q.why: Speakers give information out to the user; the others put data in.

q.q: Where are installed programs and saved files kept for the long term?
q.why: Storage keeps files and installed software for the longer term.

q.q: Which part of a computer system processes data according to its instructions, turning it into information?
q.why: The processor processes data according to the instructions it has been given.

q.q: Why is a touchscreen both an input and an output device?
o: It has a keyboard and a speaker built in
It stores data and processes it at the same time
You tap it to put data in and it shows you pictures
It connects to the internet and to a printer
q.why: You tap a touchscreen (input) and it shows you pictures (output).

q.q: In the desk and schoolbag comparison, what is memory like?
o: Your teacher: who tells you what to do next
Your desk: what you're working on now, cleared at the end of the day
Your locker: things stored safely for the whole year
Your schoolbag: things kept until you need them again
q.why: Memory is like your desk; storage is like your schoolbag or locker.

q.q: Which list contains only input devices?
q.why: Keyboards, scanners and barcode readers put data in; printers, monitors and projectors are output.

q.q: Which component does every other component plug into?
q.why: The motherboard is the main circuit board that every other component plugs into.

q.q: What is the job of the heat sink and fan?
o: Create the images sent to the monitor
Change mains electricity into low voltages
Store files when the power is off
Keep the CPU and other parts cool
q.why: They stop the CPU and other parts overheating and getting damaged.

q.q: Which component changes mains electricity into the lower voltages the parts need?
q.why: The power supply changes mains electricity into the low voltages the components need.

q.q: Which pair of components are both found inside the computer case?
q.why: RAM and the power supply are internal; keyboard, mouse, webcam and monitor are external.

q.q: Which component is often called the 'brain' of the computer?
q.why: The CPU carries out the instructions of programs and does the calculations.

q.q: What is the chassis?
o: The main circuit board that components plug into
The part that keeps the CPU cool
The case that holds and protects the internal components
The cable that carries mains electricity
q.why: The chassis is the case (frame) that holds and protects all the internal components.

q.q: Why does RAM hold the programs and data being used right now?
o: So they can be sent to the monitor
So they are kept when the power is off
So they can be backed up to the cloud
So the CPU can get them quickly
q.why: RAM holds what is in use so the CPU can get it quickly; it is wiped when the power is off.

q.q: Which component keeps the operating system and your files when the power is off?
q.why: The HDD is a storage device that keeps data when the power is off.

q.q: Which component has its own processor (GPU) to create game graphics?
q.why: The graphics card has its own GPU and memory to create images, video and game graphics.

q.q: Why do many newer computers use an SSD instead of a hard disk drive?
o: It has no moving parts, so it is faster, quieter and tougher
It holds data only while the computer is switched on
It keeps the CPU cool so it does not overheat
It changes mains electricity into lower voltages
q.why: An SSD has no moving parts, so it is faster, quieter and tougher.

q.q: Why must you never open a computer while it is plugged in?
o: The fan will stop and the CPU will overheat
The motherboard will reset all its settings
The power supply carries dangerous mains electricity
The hard disk drive will lose all its files
q.why: The power supply carries mains electricity, which is dangerous.

q.q: What does a Raspberry Pi use for storage?
q.why: A Raspberry Pi has no hard drive; it uses a microSD card slotted into the underside.

q.q: Which Raspberry Pi port would you use to connect it to a TV?
q.why: The micro HDMI ports output video and sound to TVs or monitors.

q.q: What is the Ethernet port on a Raspberry Pi for?
o: A wired network or internet connection
q.why: Ethernet is for a network cable and a wired internet connection.

q.q: Why do many games look almost the same on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X?
o: They use exactly the same controller
They both use a microSD card
They are made by the same company
q.why: Both use very similar AMD hardware under the hood.

q.q: What is the main difference between the blue USB 3 ports and the black USB 2 ports on a Raspberry Pi?
o: The USB 3 ports are for power only
The USB 3 ports are for network cables
q.why: USB 3 ports are faster, good for USB sticks and drives.

q.q: Where does the power cable plug into a Raspberry Pi?
q.why: Power plugs into the USB-C power supply port.

q.q: Why was the Raspberry Pi designed?
o: To act as a school network server
To help young people learn to program
To store files for the whole family
To replace games consoles in the home
q.why: It was designed in Cambridge to help young people learn to program.

q.q: How much RAM do both the PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X have?
q.why: Both have 16 GB GDDR6 RAM; 825 GB and 1 TB are their SSD storage.

q.q: Which statement about the PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X storage is correct?
o: The PS5 has 16 GB storage and the Xbox has 1 TB
Both store games on a microSD card
Both have a 1 TB hard disk drive
The PS5 has an 825 GB SSD and the Xbox has a 1 TB SSD
q.why: The PS5 has an 825 GB SSD; the Xbox Series X has a 1 TB SSD.

q.q: What does CPU stand for?
q.why: CPU = Central Processing Unit.

q.q: What does SSD stand for?
q.why: SSD = Solid State Drive: fast storage on memory chips with no moving parts.

q.q: What does LAN stand for?
q.why: LAN = Local Area Network: a network in one building or site.

q.q: Which acronym is a type of memory that keeps its contents when the power is off?
q.why: ROM (Read Only Memory) keeps its contents when power is off and holds start-up instructions.

q.q: What does USB stand for?
q.why: USB = Universal Serial Bus.

q.q: Which three jobs does USB do?
o: Connects devices, transfers data and supplies power
Stores files, processes data and outputs sound
Creates graphics, cools the CPU and stores data
Connects to the internet, sends email and prints
q.why: USB connects devices, transfers data and supplies power.

q.q: What is an acronym?
o: A technical word that has an American spelling
A word that is spelled the same backwards
A password made from letters and numbers
A short word made from the first letters of other words
q.why: An acronym is made from the first letters of other words.

q.q: What does HDMI stand for?
q.why: HDMI = High-Definition Multimedia Interface: carries HD video and sound.

q.q: About how much data can a DVD store?
q.why: A DVD stores about 4.7 GB; a CD stores about 700 MB.

q.q: Which acronym is an older cable or port for sending video to a monitor?
q.why: VGA (Video Graphics Array) is an older cable/port for sending video to a monitor.

q.q: Which group of acronyms are all types of storage?
q.why: HDD, SSD, CD and DVD are storage; RAM and ROM are memory, CPU and GPU are processors.

q.q: What is an algorithm?
o: A program written in a language such as Python
A diagram made of symbols joined by arrows
A sequence of instructions to complete a task or solve a problem
A location in memory that stores a value
q.why: An algorithm is a sequence of instructions, or set of rules, followed to complete a task.

q.q: Which of these is an everyday example of an algorithm?
o: A recipe for baking a cake
A list of your favourite foods
q.why: A recipe is a set of ordered steps, so it is an algorithm.

q.q: Why must an algorithm be translated into code?
o: Code lets the algorithm be printed on paper
Code makes the algorithm longer and more detailed
Algorithms only work on paper, not on screens
Computers can't understand algorithms written in English
q.why: Computers follow code written in a programming language, not English.

q.q: Which of these is a programming language named in the notes?
q.why: Scratch, Python and C# are programming languages.

q.q: What three words describe the instructions in a good algorithm?
q.why: An algorithm needs clear, short and specific instructions.

q.q: Why does the order of instructions in an algorithm matter?
o: The first step is the only one that is followed
The order only matters if there are more than ten steps
Computers read instructions from the bottom up
Doing steps in the wrong order can give the wrong result
q.why: Algorithms are a sequence; the order of the instructions matters.

q.q: Which of these is described as a complex algorithm?
o: Checking if a number is prime
Studying the pages you like to decide which adverts to show you
q.why: Deciding which adverts to show from the pages you like is complex; the others are simple.

q.q: Which is the correct sequence for starting an ICT lesson?
o: Log on, sit down quietly, search for a word, open a browser
Open a browser, log on, sit down quietly, search for a word
Sit down quietly, log on, open a browser, search for a word
Sit down quietly, open a browser, log on, search for a word
q.why: You must sit down and log on before opening a browser, and open the browser before searching.

q.q: Why might a game developer use several programming languages in one game?
o: Using one language is against the law
Each language only works on one console
Computers can only run one line of each language
q.why: Different languages suit different jobs, so developers sometimes use several in the same game.

q.q: Which flowchart shape is used for a decision?
q.why: Decisions are diamonds; rectangles are processes and parallelograms are input/output.

q.q: Which symbol would you use for 'Wait 5 minutes'?
q.why: Delays are processes, shown with a rectangle.

q.q: What is unique about the decision symbol?
o: It must always be the first symbol
It can only be used once per flowchart
It has no arrows going into it
It has two exits, Yes and No
q.why: A decision asks a yes/no question and branches two ways.

q.q: 'Input your name' would go in which shape?
q.why: Input and output use a parallelogram.

q.q: Which shape is used to start or stop a flowchart?
q.why: Start/Stop uses a rounded rectangle.

q.q: How many Start symbols should every flowchart have?
o: None, it begins with a process
q.why: Every flowchart should have exactly one Start and at least one Stop.

q.q: What is a flowchart made up of?
q.why: A flowchart is made up of symbols and arrows.

q.q: In a flowchart, what does a 'No' arrow that loops back to an earlier step do?
q.why: A No arrow that loops back makes steps repeat.

q.q: In a flowchart for running a bath, which step should be a diamond?
q.why: A question with a yes/no answer goes in a decision diamond.

q.q: Which is an advantage of computer control?
o: It still works if there is a power cut
It can work in places that are dangerous to humans
It can think of new ideas for itself
q.why: Computers can work in environments that are dangerous for people.

q.q: A computer-controlled crossing meets a situation its programmer never thought of. What is most likely to happen?
o: It will ask a police officer for help
It will handle it better than a human
It won't know what to do
It will work out a new rule for itself
q.why: Computers only follow their programming, so they can't handle conditions not covered in it.

q.q: What happens to computer-controlled traffic lights in a power cut?
o: They switch to a backup program
q.why: Computers rely on power, so in a power cut the program won't work.

q.q: A factory robot makes the same weld 10,000 times perfectly. Which advantage of computer control is this?
o: It is cheap to buy and develop
It can adapt to unexpected problems
It needs no programming at all
It can repeat actions identically indefinitely
q.why: Computers can repeat actions in an identical way indefinitely.

q.q: What is computer control?
o: Using a computer to run a system such as traffic lights
Using a password to control who logs on
A human directing traffic at a junction
A teacher controlling which websites pupils visit
q.why: Using a computer to run a system like traffic lights is computer control.

q.q: An ambulance needs to get through a busy junction. Who is better at coping with this?
o: Either, because both cope with the unexpected equally
A police officer, because a human can think and adapt
Traffic lights, because they process sensors quickly
Traffic lights, because computers never need breaks
q.why: Humans can think and adapt; computers can't cope with things not covered in their programming.

q.q: Why might an underpowered computer be a problem in a time-critical situation?
o: It might take too long to respond
It might need to take a break
It might use too little electricity
It might ask for a pay rise
q.why: Underpowered computers might take too long in a time-critical (urgent) situation.

q.q: Computers are 'only as good as their programming'. What does this mean?
o: Expensive computers never have program errors
Computers ignore their programming if it is wrong
Errors in the program cause errors in what the computer does
Computers can improve their own programs over time
q.why: A computer's programming may contain errors, and it will follow them.

q.q: Comparing costs, which is true of traffic lights compared with a police officer?
o: Traffic lights are expensive to install but need no wages
Both cost exactly the same over a year
Traffic lights are cheap to install and need weekly pay
A police officer is expensive to install but needs no wages
q.why: Traffic lights are expensive to install but have no wages; an officer needs paying every week.

q.q: What can a computer process very quickly to help control a system?
o: Situations it was not programmed for
q.why: Computers can process data from sensors very quickly and handle thousands of inputs.

q.q: Which digits does binary use?
q.why: Binary uses only 0 and 1.

q.q: X = 20, then X = X + 5. What is stored in X now?
q.why: X + 5 adds 5 to whatever is stored in X: 20 + 5 = 25.

q.q: What is a variable?
o: A named location in memory that stores a value
A fixed number that can never change
A flowchart symbol for a decision
q.why: A variable is a labelled box in memory that temporarily stores a value.

q.q: Why is 'INPUT number1, INPUT number2, answer = number1 × number2' better than 'answer = 2 × 4'?
o: It works for any numbers, so it is reusable
It is shorter and quicker to type
It does not need to use any memory
q.why: Variables make programs reusable for any numbers.

q.q: In binary, what do 0 and 1 represent, like a tiny switch?
o: 0 is true and 1 is an error
q.why: Each 0 or 1 is like a switch that is off (0) or on (1).

q.q: Score = 10. The program runs Score = Score + 5 and then Score = Score + 5 again. What is Score now?
In a game like The Sims, which of these could be stored in a Boolean (true/false) variable?
q.why: Glasses is yes/no, so true/false fits; name and hair colour are text and age is a number.

q.q: Which everyday object is a variable compared to in the notes?
q.why: A variable is like an empty box with a label on it, or a calculator's memory button.

q.q: Lives = 3. The player loses a life and the program runs Lives = Lives - 1. What is Lives now?
q.why: 3 - 1 = 2; the variable's value changes while the program runs.

q.q: How many LEDs are on the front of a micro:bit?
q.why: A 5 × 5 grid gives 25 LEDs.

q.q: Which micro:bit part detects shaking and tilting?
q.why: The accelerometer is the motion detector.

q.q: Which data type would store the value 7.5?
q.why: Numbers with a decimal point are doubles.

q.q: Which data type can only be true or false?
q.why: Booleans hold true or false.

q.q: Where is the LED with coordinates (0, 0) on a micro:bit?
q.why: LED coordinates start at (0, 0) in the top-left corner.

q.q: What are the coordinates of the bottom-right LED on a micro:bit?
q.why: Coordinates go from 0 to 4, x across and y down, so bottom-right is (4, 4).

q.q: Which LED is at (3, 1)?
o: 4th from the left, 2nd row from the bottom
3rd from the left, 1st row from the top
4th from the left, 2nd row from the top
2nd from the left, 4th row from the top
q.why: Counting from 0, x = 3 is the 4th column and y = 1 is the 2nd row, counting down from the top.

q.q: Why should a phone number be stored as a string, not an integer?
o: It starts with 0 and you never do maths with it
Integers cannot hold more than four digits
Strings use less memory than integers
q.why: A phone number starts with 0 and is never used for maths, so it is stored as text.

q.q: Which data type holds a single letter or symbol, such as 'A'?
q.why: A char holds a single letter or symbol; a string is a sequence of characters.

q.q: Which micro:bit part would let two micro:bits send messages to each other?
q.why: The radio and Bluetooth antenna connect to other micro:bits or devices wirelessly.

q.q: What type of data is "Hello ERGS!"?
q.why: Text that is a sequence of characters is a string.

q.q: What does 'loop' mean in programming?
q.why: A loop repeats code; choosing is selection.

q.q: 'repeat 4 times' is an example of which kind of loop?
q.why: We know it will repeat exactly 4 times, so it is count-controlled.

q.q: In an IF … ELSE statement, when does the ELSE part run?
o: Every time, after the IF part
Only when there is no condition
q.why: ELSE runs when the condition is not true.

q.q: Which type of loop should you use to keep asking for a password until it is correct?
q.why: We don't know how many attempts it will take, so use a condition-controlled loop.

q.q: What is a condition?
o: The first step of an algorithm
A named box that stores a value
A block of code that repeats
A test that is true or false
q.why: A condition is a test that is true or false, used to decide if code runs.

q.q: What is selection in programming?
o: Repeating a piece of code a set number of times
Putting instructions in the correct order
Storing a value in a named location in memory
Using a condition to decide if a piece of code should run
q.why: Selection uses an IF statement to decide whether code runs.

q.q: Which is another name for a loop?
q.why: Loops are also called iteration.

q.q: In a condition-controlled loop, when is the condition checked?
o: Only once, at the very start
Only after the loop has finished
q.why: The condition is checked before each repeat; when it is false the loop stops.

q.q: myValue = 0. While myValue < 3, add 1 to myValue. How many times does the loop run?
q.why: It runs with myValue 0, 1 and 2; when myValue is 3 the condition is false and it stops.

q.q: A program must flash an LED exactly 10 times. Which is the best loop to use?
q.why: When you know exactly how many repeats you need, use a count-controlled loop.

q.q: IF temperature > 30 THEN show 'Hot' ELSE show 'OK'. The temperature is 30. What is shown?
q.why: 30 is not greater than 30, so the condition is false and the ELSE part runs.
